newsitem.title: USA: USAir will not receive Airbus planes in 1997.
newsitem.headline: USAir will not receive Airbus planes in 1997.

text.p: USAir Group Inc said Thursday it would not take delivery of six Airbus Industrie aircraft in 1997 as previously expected.
"While Airbus recognizes that we are working to achieve a competitive cost structure, Airbus cannot support any 1997 deliveries," USAir said in its internal newsletter.
USAir had expected to arrange delivery of the six aircraft through leasing companies, not directly from Airbus.
USAir declined comment on whether the six-plane order was cancelled or merely delayed.

The matter will not affect a separate $5 billion USAir deal for Airbus jets announced in November. USAir has agreeed to buy 120 Airbus jets and has options for 280 more. That deal is contingent on USAir cutting its costs.
USAir and Airbus said they remain committed to the $5 billion deal.
USAir also said it seeks to buy wide-body aircraft, such as Boeing Co's 777 and Airbus A330s, but no deal has been reached.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, a Daimler-Benz AG unit, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
